subject: Fitting Negative binomial regression model in Rstan

messages.author: d6a22ac7ce11aa1b
messages.subject: Fitting Negative binomial regression model in Rstan
parts:
Hi All,

I am fitting a negative binomial model in stan, I saw in a sample code the "write(x, file='data')". I am not clearly sure what does it indicate as I am still learner in this language. 

Can I please get the clarification of these >write(negbin, file="negbin-glm.stan")    >CB<-stan_model("negbin-glm.stan") in this sample code.

Thank you.

negbin<-"
data{
int<lower=0> N;                           # rows of data
vector[N] studyperiod;
vector[N] majaadt;
vector[N] minaadt;                    # predictor variable
vector[N] majlane;
vector[N] minlane;
vector[N] medianwidth;
vector[N] speed;
vector[N] landuse;
vector[N] mediantype;
int<lower=0> totalcrashes[N];            # response variable
}

parameters {
real<lower=0> phi;      # negative binomial dispersion parameter
real beta0;             # intercept
real beta3;
real beta5;
real beta6;
real beta7;
real beta8;
real beta9;
real beta10;
real beta11;
real beta12;
}

model {
### priors
phi ~    cauchy(0.001,0.001);
beta0 ~ normal(0.0,1E4);
beta3 ~  normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta5 ~  normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta6 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta7 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta8 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta9 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta10 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta11 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta12 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
# data model
totalcrashes ~ neg_binomial_2_log(beta0 + beta3*studyperiod + beta5*majaadt + beta6*minaadt + beta7*majlane + beta8*minlane + beta9*speed + beta10*landuse + beta11*medianwidth + beta12*mediantype, phi);
}
"

write(negbin, file="negbin-glm.stan")
CB<-stan_model("negbin-glm.stan")
set.seed(1000)
N<- 276
phi<-  0.524658  
beta0<- -3.279956
beta3<- -0.0709271 
beta5<-  0.0807461
beta6<-   0.3647194
beta7<- 0.0069352
beta8<- 0.0548912
beta9<-  0.7149454
beta10<- 0.3034317 
beta11<-  0.0014502 
beta12<- -0.1764844
comparisonbefore<-sampling(CB, data=list(N=N, totalcrashes=crashdata_CB$totalcrashes, studyperiod=crashdata_CB$studyperiod, majaadt=crashdata_CB$majaadt, minaadt=crashdata_CB$minaadt, majlane=crashdata_CB$majlane, minlane=crashdata_CB$minlane, speed=crashdata_CB$speed, landuse=crashdata_CB$landuse, medianwidth=crashdata_CB$medianwidth, mediantype=crashdata_CB$mediantype), 
                          pars=c("beta0", "beta3", "beta5", "beta6", "beta7", "beta8", "beta9", "beta10", "beta11", "beta12",  "phi"),
                          iter=50000, warmup=10000, chains=4)
comparisonbefore

Hi,

That's not Stan code. 

That's R. It's just taking the variable in R called negbin and writing it to a file called negbin-glm.stan. If you open up the file, it'll have the contents of the string inside the file.


Daniel
